mapNote.en: Kosovo is not part of Serbia on the map, nor in Cliopatria. Kosovo is shown as a separate state from the declaration of independence in 2008, by decision of Historia-globen; Sweden has had diplomatic relations with Kosovo since then (Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs, checked 2026-11-06). In the years before 2008 Kosovo is shown without a state, because the area was administered by the UN and its status had not been settled.

The border is disputed. Nagorno-Karabakh and surrounding areas, which Cliopatria counts as part of Armenia, are shown without a state up to and including 2022 and as part of Azerbaijan from 2023, because the Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs writes that Azerbaijan re-established its control over Nagorno-Karabakh in the autumn of 2023 (checked 2026-11-06). The border of the area comes from Natural Earth.

The border is disputed. Cliopatria counts Nagorno-Karabakh and surrounding areas as part of Armenia. The map does not show them as Armenia: up to and including 2022 they are shown without a state, as disputed, and from 2023 as part of Azerbaijan, because the Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs writes that Azerbaijan then re-established its control over Nagorno-Karabakh (checked 2026-11-06). The area is the part of Cliopatria's Armenia that lies within Azerbaijan's border in Natural Earth.

The border is disputed. Abkhazia and South Ossetia are drawn as part of Georgia, because for disputed borders the map follows Sweden's official position: Sweden supports Georgia's territorial integrity (Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs, checked 2026-11-06). According to Natural Earth, the areas are self-governing. The map shows Georgia in 1918–1921 and from 1992, as Cliopatria does.

The border is disputed. Transnistria is drawn as part of Moldova, by decision of Historia-globen. The Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs describes Transnistria as a region of Moldova but has no stated position on the area's status that we have found (checked 2026-11-06). According to Natural Earth, the area is self-governing. Cliopatria counts Transnistria as part of Russia, as an occupied territory.

Kosovo is shown as a separate state from the declaration of independence in 2008, by decision of Historia-globen. Sweden has had diplomatic relations with Kosovo since then (Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs, checked 2026-11-06). In 2000–2007 the area is shown without a state: Kosovo was administered by the UN and its status had not been settled. Sweden concluded an agreement with the UN administration (UNMIK, SÖ 2005:29), and in 2007 negotiations on Kosovo's future status were under way (Swedish government communication 2007/08:82). Cliopatria shows Kosovo as a separate state from as early as 2000.

The island is divided. From 1976 the whole island is drawn as Cyprus, by decision of Historia-globen. Since 1974 the island has been divided by a UN-controlled buffer zone, and the area north of the zone is not controlled by the government of the Republic of Cyprus. Sweden does not recognise the independence of Northern Cyprus, in accordance with UN Security Council resolution 541 of 1983 (Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs, checked 2026-11-06). Cliopatria shows Northern Cyprus as a separate state from 1976.
